input.message:
IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT on `src/ui/wmp/library.ts`, which I am about to merge your version of.

`Track.size` is NOT the byte count of the ogg file you produced. It is consumed by the transfer dialog (`shell/Download.tsx`), which computes the whole download animation as `sizeKb / RATE_KBPS`. If you write the real file size in there, every song becomes a multi-minute progress bar.

Two things changed under you while you were working, so please align to these exact values:

1. RATE_KBPS is now 16 (the line is 128 Kbps, up from 44.6 Kbps / 5.4 KB/sec — the old rate made gamble.exe a 13-second wait, and the owner called it too slow).

2. The three tracks' authored sizes are now, and must stay:
   - demo   / 'FIRST ONE'         / length '1:48' / size '56 KB'
   - liquid / 'LIQUID SUNRISE'    / length '3:12' / size '72 KB'
   - money  / 'MONEY (CLUB MIX)'  / length '4:06' / size '88 KB'

Those give 3.5s / 4.5s / 5.5s transfers and they escalate, which is the only property that has to be true — he is getting better and his files are getting bigger.

The titles above are also load-bearing: the Cyber Cantina mail arc is already merged and his letters quote these titles, lengths and sizes by reading `trackOf(...)`. Do not rename them.

So: keep whatever real file paths/URLs your player needs as SEPARATE fields, and leave `title`, `artist`, `length` and `size` exactly as above. If your `Track` type has grown extra fields for the audio pipeline, that is fine — just don't repurpose these four.

Also please confirm in your report: the actual on-disk sizes of the transcoded ogg files, kept separate from the authored `size` strings.
